sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner as well as learned counsel appearing for the respondents.

2. The petitioner in this case had entered into a consent agreement dated 10.06.2008 to hand over the possession of the property to Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board ('KIADB' for short)
which intended to acquire the land for building airport in Bidar.
The petitioner agreed to receive `4,50,000/- per acre as the compensation for the land.

3. It is relevant to note that prior to this consent agreement, notification under Section 28(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board Act, 1966 ('KIADB Act' for short) was published on 21.09.2007.

entities.text: Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board Act, 1966
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thereafter, notification under Section 28(4) of the KIADB Act, 1966 was published on 26.03.2008.

Though the petitioner contends that notification under Section 3(1) of the KIADB Act,
1966 was not published, the respondents have produced the notification under Section 3(1) of the KIADB Act, 1966 at Annexure-R2.
The notification, however does not bear the date.
In the facts and circumstances discussed later, this Court is of the view that non mentioning of the date in the notification under Section 3(1) of the KIADB Act, 1966 is not of much consequence.
4. The petitioner was holding land bearing Sy.No.4/2 measuring 3 acre 17 gunta and he consented to sell the land measuring 2 acre 21 gunta by accepting compensation of `4,50,000/- per acre.

The records would reveal that the petitioner has filed this petition questioning the legality of the consent agreement and also the notification under Section 28(1) of the KIADB Act and Section 28(4) of the KIADB Act.

The primary contention of the petitioner is that the consent agreement is obtained by practicing fraud and it is further contended that after notification under Section 28(1) of the KIADB Act, the award is not passed and compensation is not paid within five years from the date of commencement of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 Act. ( 'Act of 2013' for short)
5.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that being aware that the property is acquired in terms of the notification as well as the consent agreement, the petitioner has sold the property to a third party purchaser under the registered sale deed dated 06.07.2022 i.e., during the pendency of this writ petition.

Thereafter,
the purchaser filed the writ petition No.202500/2022 challenging the formation of industrial layout in the property purchased by him.
The said petition was dismissed by this Court following the law laid down by the Apex court in the case of Delhi Development Authority vs. Manpreet Singh and others [2023 SCC Online SC 29].

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority vs. Manpreet Singh and others [2023 SCC Online SC 29]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel Sri Ravi B.Patil, appearing for the petitioner urged that the purpose for which the property was acquired was to build an airport and the property is not utilized for the purpose.
Thereafter without necessary approval and without following the proper procedure, the land is converted for industrial purpose.
Since the purpose of acquisition is not achieved the entire land acquisition proceeding is vitiated is the submission.

7. It is his further contention that the consent agreement executed by the petitioner is also vitiated by fraud and the petitioner was not adequately informed about the consequences of the consent agreement and also the market value payable in respect of this particular land.

sentences.text: It is also urged that in view of the commencement of 2013 Act, the land acquisition proceedings would lapse in terms of Section 24 of the Act of 2013.

It is further urged that the compensation has to be determined with reference to the market value that has to be awarded by applying the guidelines under the Act of 2013, given the fact that the compensation is not yet paid and the possession of the land is not yet taken.

9. It is further urged that before forming industrial layout approval ought to have been taken by the competent authority as the airport project for which the land was sought to be acquired was dropped.
Since there is change in the purpose for which the land is sought to be utilised, unless there is approval by the competent authority, the land could not have been utilised for industrial purpose.

10. The learned counsel for respondent - KIADB would contend that notification under Section 3(1)
of the KIADB Act is issued declaring the land in question as the industrial land and thereafter notifications under Section 28(1) and Section 28(4) of the KIADB Act have been duly published.

It is further stated that the petitioner has voluntarily entered into a consent agreement and agreed to receive `4,50,000/- per acre as compensation in respect of the land owned by the petitioner which is sought to be acquired through consent.

11. It is also the contention of the learned counsel for the respondent that the petitioner having sold the property during the pendency of this petition cannot raise the contention relating to validity of the acquisition of land and cannot maintain the petition.
The petitioner's conduct does not entitle the petitioner for any relief prayed in the writ petition.

12. It is also the contention of the learned counsel for KIADB, that the communication was also addressed to the petitioner to receive the compensation in terms of the consent agreement vide communication dated 30.03.2013 and he has not chosen to receive the compensation.
On the other hand, seven years after entering to consent agreement has chosen to file the writ petition on the ground of fraud and misrepresentation.
13. It is also contended on behalf of the respondents that the provisions of 2013 Act are not applicable to the case on hand as the land is not acquired under the provisions of Act of 1894.
The land is acquired under the provisions of KIADB Act that too through a consent agreement, as such the provision of Section 24 of the Act of 2013 cannot be made applicable to this case.
14. This court has considered the rival contentions raised at the bar.
15. Annexure-R1 is the notification issued under Section 3(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act, 1966.
The notification though is not dated, reveals that the certain lands mentioned in the said notification including the land of the petitioner are notified as industrial lands.

That being the position, once the notification is issued under Section 3(1) of the KIADB Act,
then under Section 28 of KIADB Act, the competent authority is authorised to issue the notifications for the purpose of acquisition of land to establish the industry or to form industrial layout.
The industrial layout is formed in the lands acquired under the notifications.
This being the position it Narasareddi S/O Pentareddi vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 9 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108269060/

sentences.text: 4 cannot be contended that the lands are not acquired for the purpose set out in the KIADB Act.

Acquisition of land for industrial purpose is very much the core object of the KIADB Act.
16.

The learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4 would submit that by referring to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of P.Narayanappa and another vs. State of Karnataka and others [(2006) 7 Supreme Court Cases 578] the airport which was initially intended in the lands acquired would come under the definition of industrial infrastructure facilities and the Board was competent to acquire the land for the purpose of airport.

entities.text: P.Narayanappa and another vs. State of Karnataka and others [(2006) 7 Supreme Court Cases 578]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Later some other lands are acquired for the purpose of building airport, as such, the decision is taken to drop the proposal to construct the airport in the acquired lands.

However, since the notification was already notified under Section 3(1) of the KIADB Act, the lands notified under the said notification retained the characteristics of industrial lands and the KIADB is within its power to develop - 10 - the industrial estate in the said land and having developed the industrial estate in the said land, the petitioner cannot raise a grievance seven years after entering into consent agreement to sell the land in favour of KIADB.
17. This court finds that merely because the decision is taken to drop the airport that does not enable the petitioner to raise a contention that the entire proceedings has to be quashed.

As long as notification under Section 3(1) of the KIADB Act is not questioned by the petitioner, the petitioner cannot question the decision of the KIADB to form the industrial layout in the aforementioned land which is notified under Sections 3(1), 28(1) and 28(4) of the KIADB Act.
18 . It is also to be noticed that the petitioner has given a consent in terms of consent agreement dated 10.06.2008.
The petition is filed in the year 2015.
Till 2015, the petitioner has not raised any grievance relating to the alleged fraud, misrepresentation.

The contention relating to fraud,
misrepresentation and coercion cannot be considered in the writ jurisdiction.

It is also relevant to note that this petition is filed only in the year 2015 i.e., after the - 11 - commencement of Act of 2013, probably with an intention to take shelter under Section 24 of the Act of 2013.
19.

It is now well-settled proposition of law that the provisions of Act of 2013 are not applicable to the proceedings under KIADB Act, vide judgment of Apex Court in the case of Special land acquisition officer, KIADB vs. Anasuya Bai and others reported in (2017) 3 SCC 313 and also M.Nagabhushana vs. State of Karnataka and others reported in (2011) 3 SCC 408.

entities.text: Special land acquisition officer, KIADB vs. Anasuya Bai and others reported in (2017) 3 SCC 313
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: M.Nagabhushana vs. State of Karnataka and others reported in (2011) 3 SCC 408
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This being the position, the petitioner cannot contend that the land acquisition proceeding would lapse.
20. It is also required to be noticed that under Section 28(4) of KIADB Act, the land would vest with the Government the moment the notification under the said provision.

The Section 28(4)

sentences.text: Thus, the petitioner cannot contend that the possession is not taken by the KIADB within five years from the date of commencement of Act of 2013.
21. As already noticed the petitioner has sold the property during the pendency of this petition.
The petition is - 12 - filed challenging the acquisition of the property.
Since, the petitioner was aware that the property was acquired, the present petition is filed.
However, the petitioner has chosen to sell the property though he is not the owner.
For this reason also, this Court is of the view that the petitioner cannot be heard for considering the claim of the petitioner.
22. Learned counsel for the petitioner has referred to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kedar Nath Yadav vs. State of West Bengal and others [(2017) 11 Supreme Court Cases 601).

entities.text: Kedar Nath Yadav vs. State of West Bengal and others [(2017) 11 Supreme Court Cases 601)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The facts obtained in the said case are totally different from the facts in the present case.
And it is also relevant to note that the Apex Court in the above said case has exercised the power under Article 142 of Constitution of India and such power cannot be exercised in this jurisdiction.
It is also required to be noticed that KIADB has already developed the land and certain plots are already allotted to certain persons.
Under these circumstances, this Court finds that there is no merit in the petition and accordingly the petition is rejected.
In view of disposal of petition, all pending interlocutory applications do not survive for consideration.
Accordingly, dismissed.
